chapter: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
title: Chorus girls and learning to play for entertainers at the Apex
summary: Life at 16 or 17 among chorus girls, and how the floor-show job taught Royal to accompany entertainers' moods.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We left you with the chorus line (inaudible) at the Apex Club.

Well, that was a lot of fun. It was my first experience that really being around real women. You know, I was actually a child. I was 16, 17-year-old child, going to work with men. Although I'd always worked around men, this was my first real good contact with real women. When you start getting broke into true life with chorus girls, some of them are real women because of different facts that happen in their lives. It's a rough life for a chorus girl, so there's many experiences that can be derived from being correctly broken in.
Except that (inaudible) it's not quite possible today; there aren't very many chorus girls.

No, there are no chorus girls, no. It's a thing of the past. It was a lot of fun. But getting away from the chorus girls, the Apex as a club was a wonderful thing for me in my life of education because they had a first-class show there, with the best entertainers available and when they didn't have them, they sent East for them and had them sent out to perform for Curtis Moseby. It was my experience to learn how to play shows, how to be sensitive toward

entertainers as to their whims and their ways of deliveries and how they felt on this particular night and how they felt on the next night and being able to be conscious of exactly what was happening in the -- in their particular line of work. It taught you how to learn how to play a tune a half-step away tonight if he's hoarse and play it a little bit slower tonight if they're tired and a little bit faster tomorrow night, if they're feeling better and if they'd had a little taste of something and felt like kicking it a little bit higher, it also showed you how to do that. It was a wonderful education.
